lines.arrive: Crossing a heath, on a grey morning.
lines.stone: How did it get here? For all you know, it has always been here.
lines.stone_look: Just a stone. Nobody would ask who made it.
lines.watch: And there, in the heather: a watch.
lines.parts: Springs and wheels, each one cut to fit the next. A balance swinging back and forth. All of it, for telling the time.
lines.maker: Even if you'd never seen a watch before, you'd know: someone made this.
lines.hare: A hare, watching you. Its eye focuses, and adjusts to the light, and keeps itself clean.
lines.eye: And the hare watching you from the gorse has an eye far finer than any watch.
lines.ask: So did someone make the hare, too?
lines.maker_1: A workshop, with the lamp still lit. Whoever works here has only just stepped out.
lines.maker_2: Something so well fitted to its purpose: it's hard to believe that nobody meant it.
lines.pond_1: Tiny creatures, each a little different from its parents. The ones that sense the light a little better leave a few more young.
lines.pond_2: A patch that feels the light. A cup. A deeper cup. A pinhole. A lens.
lines.pond_3: Nobody meant any of it. There was just a great deal of time, and some ways of living that worked a little better than others.
lines.hume_1: You've seen watches made. You've never seen a world made.
lines.walk_on: You put the watch in your pocket, and walk on.
lines.hume_2: Maybe the world is more like a plant than a watch. Or maybe it had many makers, or a clumsy one. From one watch, how could you tell?
